text:
Elyse: CI perf alert on longctx bench — runtime/e2e/linux-gpu-large failed with OOM + sustained token latency regression. Saw this on the nightly perf dashboard: memory climbs and then CUDA OOMs at seqlen=8192. Suspect allocator change from last week (PR 0a1b2c3).
ci-bot: ci/perf-longctx (gpu-large) failed — job 4821 — peak GPU mem 14.6GB, OOM at step 42.
Diego: I noticed similar on dedicated yesterday after the allocator-refactor landed. Heap fragmentation looked suspicious in the vm maps.
Matt: quick bisect shows the regression introduced by commit 0a1b2c3 (allocator: slab pooling refactor). It changed the fallback path to use `cudaHostAlloc` -> causing some slabs to be page-locked host memory then remapped, which increases memcpy and fragments GPU address space.
Olivia: repro steps I used: `./scripts/run_longctx_bench --model redwood-v1 --seqlen 8192 --batch 1 --kv-cache-size 12G` — repro is reliable on linux-gpu-large.
Diego: repro output snippet: ```[2026-11-03T14:21:07Z] alloc_slab: requested 2097152 bytes, returned ptr 0x7fb13c000000 (host-mapped)
[2026-11-03T14:21:07Z] cudaMemcpyAsync host->device 2097152 bytes took 24.3ms (expected ~0.6ms)
[2026-11-03T14:21:08Z] WARNING: KV cache fragmentation: free_fragments=37 total_free=3.2G contiguous_max=128M
[2026-11-03T14:21:09Z] ERROR: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory
```
Matt: profiling (ncu) shows a 3x increase in host->device memcpy time for slab-backed allocations vs directly cudaMalloc'd device slabs. That explains the token latency regression. Also kernel selection falls back to safe (non-quant) kernel when pointers aren't device-aligned.
Elyse: so two fold: (1) higher memcpy cost -> latency regression in perf CI; (2) fragmentation -> OOMs at long seqlen. Both triggered by slab allocation path change.
Olivia: can we add a quick guard in `gpu_allocator` to prefer `cudaMalloc` for slabs above X size or when contiguous space needed? Also add a flag `--prefer_device_slab` to repro.
Diego: workaround pushed locally: force device allocation for slabs >= 1MB. Reprobench passes now. I'll open a revert PR for 0a1b2c3 and include a proper allocator test that simulates high seqlen KV allocation patterns.
Matt: please include a perf test that asserts host->device memcpy percentile stays < 1ms for typical slab ops. We need this in CI to catch regressions.
Elyse: @Diego assign the revert and tag infra/ci so we can add the perf gate. This is a rollout-blocker for next week's deploy. :warning:
Diego: creating PR now: `revert: allocator-refactor (0a1b2c3) + slab-alignment-test`. Linking here when ready.
ci-bot: triggered: run `perf-longctx` on branch diego/allocator-revert (job queued).
Matt: also add metrics to console: slab_backed_count, avg_memcpy_ms, largest_contiguous_free. If those spike we'll auto-hold rollouts.
Olivia: I'll add the extra perf job to the matrix and run an expanded seqlen sweep (2048/4096/8192).
Elyse: thanks all. Once PR is up we'll run the e2e on dedicated and hold the release until perf passes.
sre-bot: Incident created: "kv-slab-shifting-mem-regression" assigned to Diego. Priority=P1.
Diego: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2215 — reverting allocator-refactor and adding slab alignment + perf test. Running CI now. :shipit: 
Matt: +1 on the revert. After revert, follow-up ticket to reintroduce pooling but preserve device-first slab allocation and add a fallback that doesn't pin host memory unless necessary.
Elyse: update: CI run on revert branch passed longctx perf (no OOMs, memcpy p50 0.58ms). Marking rollout hold released after manual check. Thanks team. :tada:
